line: - **sprint-folder** One branch and folder per Sprint, scrum/sprint-NN-<suffix>/; the tag has the same name. Read details/sprint.md first.
note: 'With a separate working copy if wanted' is dropped (optional); the folder layout under scrum/ is in the folders long file.

line: - **no-end-date** A Sprint closes when its goal is met or the PO stops it; the PO watches for one that drags on (departs from the Guide).
note: The reason for the departure stays in the departures long file.

line: - **small-sprint** Even half an hour of work gets a Sprint, each step a line or two; stage gates, review and close still apply.
note: The old '(convention 24)' becomes the handle stage-gates.

lines: - **sprint-goal** [po,sm] The PO sets the Sprint Goal in their own style, usually with the Scrum Master: one unifying value goal.
- **share-goal-and-checks** [po,sm] Share the Sprint Goal and the checks to focus on with the Scrum Master and the Developer.
where_else: The summary-Sprint exception (several lines of work in one single-line commitment cell), the pointer to the full Definition of Done in section 1.3 and 'leaving out a check does not waive a standard' are in plugins/ideo-scrum/template/sprint-backlog-template.md (lines 16, 20) and in dod-in-product-log.
note: The ideo-kernel fallback sentence is dropped (explanation).

line: - **select-items** [po,sm] Copy items into 2.1 word for word; each serves the Sprint Goal: add a missing one to the product log first; never pad.
note: The five columns and word-for-word copy are in the sprint log template (lines 26-28). This is the line product-log#12 refers to.

line: - **refinement** [sm,po] The Scrum Master leads refinement with the PO; seven steps; the PO says when it is over. Read details/refinement.md first.
note: Long file: the seven steps word for word, what is written into section 2.2 (what was settled and who decided, acceptance criteria, tests), and step 4's pointer to the design-sprint-or-five-modes boundary as the sprint-or-modes handle.

lines: - **how-is-a-plan** [dev] The How is a plan of work items, each done in one session, with an output and a done test. Read details/sprint.md first.
- **no-steps** [dev] Keep the How at the level of approach: no steps, no file contents, no polishing; if you can write the steps, do the work.
where_else: What the How holds (key choices and reasons, known risks and open points) is in the sprint log template (line 37) and commands/developer.md (line 33).
note: The departure (the Scrum Guide's 'one day or less' becomes one session) is in the sprint-stages long file, where the rule is kept in full, and in the departures table. 'The Scrum Master and the PO check the plan' is covered elsewhere (review-handover, the role commands) and not repeated.

lines: - **go-ahead** Build only on the PO's go-ahead, with its date and reach (commit … push); approving a plan is not one. Read details/sprint.md first.
- **review-handover** [po,sm] The PO may hand the review of the How, new structures and full texts to the Scrum Master in writing; not the go-ahead.
note: A thing the PO stopped in an earlier Sprint, so both halves stay.

lines: - **increment-notes** [dev] Keep chapter 4 as the full record: a new session goes by the notes alone and does not work everything out again.
- **mark-done** [dev] Mark a finished work item by prefixing its Done when cell with ✓ <date>, keeping the condition; an unmarked row is not done.
where_else: That the notes take any form and that chapter 4 may refine the How is in the sprint log template (line 50).
note: The board reads the done mark (board-log, and the board check script), so mark-done must stay in the list.
